responsibilities.duty: Ensures every file is complete; schedules and tracks TB screening; manages exposure reports and return-to-work clearances; audits files.
Complete evaluations on time; do not knowingly allow exposed or diagnosed employees to serve clients; refer reports to the Administrator.
Provide accurate information; complete screening on time; report exposure or diagnosis immediately; update contact information.

documentation: Personnel file with the nine required items
TB screening results and annual tracker
Targeted screening and exposure reports
Return-to-work clearance statements
Bonding or universal bond documentation
Annual performance evaluations
Orientation and training records
Personnel file audit results

policies.title: Staffing Sufficiency and Unexpected Staff Shortages
policies.applies_to: Administrator, scheduling staff, RN Supervisor, intake staff and all caregivers
policies.purpose: To make sure the agency has enough qualified staff to deliver the services promised in every service agreement, and to protect clients when an unexpected staff shortage occurs.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.09(5) (Staffing). [AGENCY NAME] maintains sufficient numbers of qualified staff, as required by the rules, to provide the services specified in its service agreements with clients. The agency does not accept a new client or add hours unless caregivers who are qualified for the tasks are available. If the agency becomes aware that it is unable to deliver the specified services to a client because of an unexpected staff shortage, it advises the client and refers the client to another provider if the client so desires. The notice and referral are documented in the client record.

definitions.definition: Employees who meet the qualifications for the tasks they are assigned (nursing license under ADM-10; PCA qualifications under ADM-11; companion/sitter requirements under ADM-12), have a satisfactory fingerprint determination, and have completed orientation and the written competency evaluation (ADM-09).

A situation in which the agency learns it cannot staff services in a service agreement, for example because of resignations, illness, no-shows, or loss of a qualified caregiver, and cannot arrange coverage.
Giving the client the names and contact information of other licensed providers, and, with the client's consent, assisting with the transfer of needed information.

procedures: Before accepting any new client or increase in hours, the intake coordinator and scheduler confirm in writing that qualified caregivers (and the RN Supervisor, if nursing is involved) are available for the days, times and tasks in the proposed service agreement. If capacity is not available, the client is not accepted and is referred elsewhere (ADM-01, OPS-01).

The Administrator maintains a capacity report showing, by week, the hours committed in service agreements versus hours that qualified, available staff can cover, including needs for special conditions competencies (ADM-11). The report is reviewed weekly.
The scheduler maintains a list of qualified back-up caregivers (cross-trained staff and part-time or on-call employees) and keeps current contact information.
Employees must notify the scheduler as early as possible, and at least [NUMBER] hours before a shift when feasible, if they cannot work. Call-outs are logged with date, reason and coverage arranged.

When a caregiver is unavailable, the scheduler first tries to fill the visit with a qualified back-up caregiver and confirms that the substitute is qualified for the tasks and has been introduced to the service plan (PLN-01).
If no qualified coverage can be arranged, the scheduler notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator decides whether the shortage is a short-term gap or a continuing problem.

The Administrator or designee contacts the client (and responsible party, where applicable) by telephone as soon as the shortage is known, before the scheduled visit whenever possible, and no later than the start of the scheduled visit. The call explains which services cannot be delivered and for how long.

The caller asks whether the client wishes to be referred to another provider. If yes, the agency gives at least [NUMBER] names of other licensed providers or the local Area Agency on Aging contact, with consent shares needed information, and cooperates in the transition (OPS-03).

If the client prefers to wait, the agency continues to seek coverage and agrees on a revised schedule with the client. The agency does not leave a client with high-risk needs without care: the RN Supervisor assesses urgent needs and arranges emergency coverage or alternatives (SAF-07, OPS-02).
For waiver clients (CCSP/SOURCE, ICWP, NOW/COMP), the Administrator also notifies the case manager or support coordinator of the shortage and any referral, as the program requires (OPS-04).

The Administrator documents in the client record each shortage notice: date and time, who was notified, the services affected, the client's decision on referral, any referral given, and the follow-up.

If a shortage continues more than [NUMBER] days or affects more than one client, the Administrator develops a staffing recovery plan (recruiting, overtime within wage rules under PER-02, temporary hold on new admissions) and records it.
The Administrator submits shortage events, missed visits and resulting complaints to the Quality Improvement program quarterly (SVC-10) and reports trends to the Governing Body (GB-01).

responsibilities.duty: Approves admissions against capacity; reviews capacity reports; notifies clients or approves notices; ensures referral and documentation; develops recovery plans.
Verifies capacity before new admissions; maintains back-up list; fills shifts with qualified staff; escalates shortages immediately.
Assesses clients' urgent needs during a shortage and approves coverage for clients with special conditions or medical frailty.
Report absences early; do not leave a client without arranging for coverage through the scheduler.

documentation: Weekly capacity report
Call-out and coverage log
Shortage notices and referral offers in the client record
Staffing recovery plans
Quality Improvement reports on shortages

policies.title: Hiring Qualifications and Written Competency Evaluation
policies.applies_to: Administrator, hiring supervisors, RN Supervisor, and all employees
policies.purpose: To ensure every employee meets minimum hiring qualifications and has a written competency evaluation, based on a supervisor's personal observation, in the personnel file.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.09(5)(a) (Staffing: written evaluation and minimum qualifications). [AGENCY NAME] keeps in the personnel record of every employee a written evaluation showing that the employee's performance of required job tasks was personally observed by a supervisor, by demonstration or direct observation, and that the performance was determined to be competent for all job tasks the employee is required to perform. All staff hired by the agency must meet these minimum qualifications: (1) prior to serving as a direct access employee, obtain a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination in compliance with the Rules and Regulations for Criminal Background Checks, Chapter 111-8-12; (2) participate in the orientation and training required by the rules; and (3) not have made any material false statement about qualification requirements to DCH or to the agency. The agency also does not hire or retain anyone with credible evidence of abuse or exploitation of a client. The agency will confirm with the Healthcare Facility Regulation Division (HFRD) which positions beyond the owner, administrator and direct access employees require fingerprint determinations, and will apply the stricter approach until it has confirmation.

definitions.definition: An employee or contractor who has direct physical access to clients in the course of duties, as defined by Chapter 111-8-12 and confirmed with HFRD.
The satisfactory determination issued under Chapter 111-8-12 after fingerprint-based criminal records checks, kept in the personnel record.

A signed, dated form completed by a supervisor who personally observed the employee perform each required job task, by actual performance with a client or by return demonstration, and recorded the determination of competent or not yet competent.
An untrue statement about licenses, certifications, training, experience or other qualifications that would affect hiring or assignment.

procedures: Before making a job offer, the hiring supervisor confirms that the applicant meets the position's qualifications (nursing license under ADM-10; PCA qualifications under ADM-11; companion/sitter requirements under ADM-12) and obtains a written application with a five-year employment history.

The hiring supervisor checks references and verifies credentials directly with the issuing source. The Administrator checks for credible evidence of abuse or exploitation, including the applicable registry checks (PER-01), and does not hire anyone with such evidence.

Each applicant signs a statement that all information about qualifications is true and that a material false statement is grounds for refusal to hire or termination. Staff who learn of a false statement report it to the Administrator, who investigates and documents the outcome.

The Administrator submits the fingerprint request under Chapter 111-8-12 for each applicant for a direct access position and does not assign the person to any client contact until a satisfactory determination is in the personnel file (PER-01).

The Administrator contacts HFRD to confirm which positions beyond the owner, administrator and direct access employees need fingerprint determinations, records the answer, date and person spoken to, and applies it to office, scheduling and billing staff.
The new employee completes orientation (ADM-13) and the required training for the position (ADM-11 or ADM-14) before working with clients unsupervised.

The RN Supervisor or another qualified supervisor builds a competency checklist from the position's job description listing every task the employee will perform, including any special-conditions tasks.

The supervisor personally observes the employee perform each task listed, by demonstration (return demonstration with a mannequin, peer or client) or by direct observation with a client, and signs and dates the determination for each task. A task not observed as competent may not be assigned.

If the employee is not yet competent in a task, the supervisor documents the gap, provides training and repeats the observation. The employee does not perform that task until competence is documented.

The completed written competency evaluation is filed in the personnel record before the employee is assigned unsupervised work. New tasks added later require a new observation and signature before assignment.
At least annually, each employee is re-evaluated in writing by direct observation or demonstration (SVC-04). The Administrator tracks due dates and removes overdue tasks from assignments.

Once a quarter the Administrator audits a sample of personnel files for fingerprint determination, orientation, training, competency evaluation and false-statement attestation, and records and corrects any gaps within 14 days.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures hiring standards are met; submits fingerprint requests; confirms scope of required checks with HFRD; audits files.
Verifies qualifications and references; ensures no assignment before determination, orientation and competency evaluation.
Personally observes and documents competency for every required task.
Provide truthful information; complete orientation and training; perform tasks only when found competent.

documentation: Application with five-year employment history
Reference and credential verifications
Signed qualifications attestation
Fingerprint records check determination
HFRD confirmation notes on covered positions
Orientation and training records
Written competency evaluation with task-by-task observation
Annual re-evaluations
Quarterly personnel file audit

policies.title: Nursing Personnel Licensure
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor, hiring staff, all nursing employees and contracted nurses
policies.purpose: To ensure that all nursing services are provided only by nurses currently licensed in Georgia and supervised by a fully licensed Georgia registered nurse.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.09(5)(b) (Nursing Personnel). Any person employed or contracted by [AGENCY NAME] to provide nursing services must be licensed in Georgia in accordance with professional licensing laws and rules (as a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse). Licensed nurses may also provide any other types of private home care services the agency offers, including personal care and companion or sitter tasks. The agency does not advertise or provide nursing services unless it employs a fully licensed Georgia registered nurse supervisor (Rule 111-8-65-.10(2)(a); see SVC-01). A nurse whose license is expired, suspended, revoked or otherwise not in good standing may not perform nursing services.

definitions.definition: Services that under Georgia professional licensing law may be performed only by a licensed nurse, such as nursing assessment, skilled treatments and nursing judgment.
Holding a current, active Georgia license (or a valid multistate license recognized in Georgia under licensing law) to practice as an RN or LPN, in good standing.
The fully licensed Georgia registered nurse the agency employs to supervise nursing services.

procedures: The Administrator confirms before advertising or offering nursing services that a fully licensed Georgia RN supervisor is employed, and records the RN's name, license number and hire date. See SVC-01.
During recruitment, the hiring supervisor identifies positions that involve nursing services and requires proof of a current Georgia nursing license (RN or LPN) from the applicant.

Before the first day of work, the Administrator verifies the license directly with the Georgia licensing authority's primary-source verification, prints or saves the result showing license number, status, expiration date and any discipline, and files it in the personnel record.
A nurse is not scheduled for any nursing service until the verification is on file and shows an active license in good standing.
The Administrator records every nurse's license expiration date on a license tracker and reviews it monthly. Nurses must give the Administrator proof of renewal before their license expires.

At each renewal, the Administrator verifies the renewed license with the licensing authority and files the new verification. If proof is not received by the expiration date, the nurse is immediately taken off nursing assignments, and the scheduler arranges coverage under ADM-08.

Nurses must report to the Administrator within 24 hours any disciplinary action, restriction, investigation, suspension or lapse of their license. The Administrator reviews the facts, decides on assignment limits or removal, and documents the decision.
Nurses may also perform personal care and companion or sitter tasks within their job description, after the competency evaluation for those tasks is complete (ADM-09).

For any nursing services delivered by a contract nurse or staffing source, the written contract requires a current Georgia license and gives the agency the right to verify it before assignment and at renewal (ADM-15).

If the agency has no RN supervisor, for example because the RN resigns, the Administrator stops accepting nursing clients immediately, arranges for continued nursing care with a licensed provider or an interim RN, and notifies HFRD as required (LIC-06).
The Administrator audits the license tracker against the personnel files quarterly and records the results.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies licenses at hire and renewal; maintains tracker; removes nurses with lapsed licenses; ensures an RN supervisor is employed.
Supervises nursing services; keeps own license current; reports concerns about nurse practice to the Administrator.
Keep license active; report discipline or lapse within 24 hours; practice only within the license.
Assigns nursing services only to nurses with verified, active licenses.

documentation: Primary-source license verifications at hire and each renewal
License expiration tracker
Disciplinary or lapse reports and Administrator decisions
Contract nurse agreements
Quarterly tracker audit

policies.title: Personal Care Assistant (PCA) Qualifications and 40-Hour Training Program
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor/Training Director, hiring staff, scheduler, and all personal care assistants
policies.purpose: To ensure that every personal care assistant has the required training and demonstrated competency before performing personal care tasks, and that PCAs are never assigned tasks or special-conditions clients for which they are not trained and competent.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.09(5)(c) (Personal Care Assistant): [AGENCY NAME] may have PCAs perform personal care tasks for clients. PCAs may also perform companion or sitter tasks but may not provide nursing services unless qualified under Rule .09(5)(b) (ADM-10). This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.09(5)(c)1: every PCA hired must have at least one of the following: (i) successful completion of a nurse aide training and competency evaluation program under 42 CFR Part 483, Subpart D; (ii) successful completion of a nurse aide competency examination recognized by DCH; (iii) successful completion of a health care or personal care credentialing program recognized and approved by DCH; or (iv) successful completion of, or progress in completing, the agency's 40-hour training program covering at least: (I) ambulation and transfer of clients, including positioning; (II) assistance with bathing, toileting, grooming, shaving, dental care, dressing and eating; (III) basic first aid and CPR; (IV) caring for clients with special conditions and needs, within the scope of tasks authorized to be performed by demonstration; (V) home management; (VI) home safety and sanitation; (VII) infection control in the home; (VIII) medically related activities, including taking vital signs; and (IX) proper nutrition. This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.09(5)(c)2: the 40-hour program is conducted under the direction of a licensed registered professional nurse or a health care professional with commensurate education and experience; twenty hours must be completed before the PCA serves clients, and the remaining twenty hours must be completed within six months of the date the training initially began; no PCA is assigned a task for which training is not completed and competency is not determined; and no PCA is assigned to care for a client with special conditions unless the PCA has received training and demonstrated competency in the services related to those special conditions.

definitions.definition: An employee who performs personal care tasks for clients and who is not performing nursing services.
The agency's PCA training course directed by an RN or equivalent professional that covers the nine required subject areas.
The date the PCA first attended the 40-hour program. The six-month completion deadline for the remaining 20 hours runs from this date.
Client conditions or needs, such as dementia, ventilator or catheter care, wounds, or complex mobility needs, that require specific training before a PCA may care for the client.
A supervisor's documented finding, after personal observation by demonstration or direct observation, that the PCA can perform a task correctly and safely.

procedures: At hiring, the Administrator determines which qualification pathway the PCA applicant meets: (i) a Part 483, Subpart D nurse aide program; (ii) a DCH-recognized nurse aide competency exam; (iii) a DCH-approved health care or personal care credential; or (iv) the agency's 40-hour program.

For pathways (i) through (iii), the Administrator obtains a copy of the certificate, registry entry or transcript, verifies it with the issuing source or the applicable registry, and files it in the personnel record. If unsure whether a credential is recognized or approved by DCH, the Administrator asks HFRD in writing before accepting it.

For pathway (iv), the Administrator enrolls the PCA in the agency's 40-hour program and records the training start date on a training tracker. The tracker shows the date by which the remaining 20 hours are due (six months from the start date).

The agency's 40-hour program is directed by [TRAINING DIRECTOR NAME], a licensed registered nurse (or a health care professional with commensurate education and experience). The director's license or credential and experience are filed in the Administrator's records. All content is approved by this director.

The curriculum includes the nine required areas (ambulation and transfer including positioning; bathing, toileting, grooming, shaving, dental care, dressing and eating; first aid and CPR; special conditions; home management; home safety and sanitation; infection control in the home; medically related activities including vital signs; and nutrition). The hours per topic are listed in the written curriculum.

Each PCA must complete at least 20 hours of the program before serving any client. The training director signs the attendance record showing dates, hours, topics and instructors, and the Administrator confirms the 20 hours are complete before the PCA is placed on the schedule.

The PCA must complete the remaining 20 hours within six months of the training start date. At 60 and 30 days before the deadline, the Administrator reviews the tracker and schedules the training. A PCA who has not completed the full 40 hours by the deadline is removed from client assignments until the program is complete.

Before assigning any task, the RN Supervisor or another qualified supervisor confirms that training on the task is complete and personally observes the PCA perform it, by demonstration or direct observation, and signs the competency determination (ADM-09). The scheduler may assign only tasks listed as competent.

The RN Supervisor reviews each client's service plan to identify tasks and special conditions (PLN-01). If a client has special conditions, the scheduler assigns only PCAs whose files show specific training and demonstrated competency for those conditions.

If no PCA with the required special-conditions competency is available, the Administrator arranges training and competency evaluation, assigns a licensed nurse, or follows ADM-08 (advise the client and refer if the client wishes). A PCA is never assigned to the client without the required competency.

PCAs may perform personal care tasks and companion or sitter tasks (SVC-02, SVC-03). The Administrator and RN Supervisor ensure PCAs do not perform nursing services, such as tasks reserved for licensed nurses (SVC-01).

The Administrator files in the personnel record the credential or the 40-hour program attendance, the competency determinations, the training director's sign-off and the special-conditions training records.

Each year the RN Supervisor reviews all PCA records against the tracker and the schedule, confirms that no PCA performed a task or served a special-conditions client without documented training and competency, and reports findings to the Quality Improvement program (SVC-10).

responsibilities.duty: Verifies pathway and credentials; maintains the training tracker; enforces the 20-hour and six-month deadlines; ensures nothing is assigned without competency.
Directs the 40-hour program; approves curriculum; observes and signs competency determinations; identifies special-conditions needs.
Assigns only tasks and clients for which the PCA's file shows completed training and competency.
Complete required training on time; perform only tasks authorized and for which competency is documented; speak up if asked to do a task without training.

documentation: Credential or certificate copies and verifications
40-hour program curriculum, instructor credentials and attendance records
Training start date and six-month deadline tracker
Task-by-task competency determinations
Special-conditions training and competency records
Annual audit of PCA assignments

policies.title: Companions and Sitters
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor/Supervisors, and all companions and sitters employed by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure that every companion or sitter [AGENCY NAME] uses is qualified, is limited to companion or sitter tasks unless separately qualified as a nurse or Personal Care Assistant (PCA), and has documented training or competency before serving clients.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] may use companions or sitters to perform companion or sitter tasks for clients. This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.09(5)(d)1-2 (Companions or Sitters). (1) Rule .09(5)(d)1: A companion or sitter may not provide any other private home care service, including personal care tasks or nursing, unless he or she is also qualified as a nurse or a PCA under the rules and the agency's policies ADM-10 and ADM-11. (2) Rule .09(5)(d)2(i): Every companion or sitter hired must be able to read and write, follow verbal and written instructions, and complete written reports and documents. (3) Rule .09(5)(d)2(ii): Every companion or sitter must, before working with clients, either successfully complete training or demonstrate understanding and practical competency in all seven required areas: the needs and characteristics of elderly, handicapped or convalescing individuals; meal preparation and serving; transportation and escort services; housekeeping, including sanitation; home safety; handling medical emergencies in the home; and infection control. Training or the competency demonstration is documented in the personnel file. A companion or sitter who has not met every requirement is not assigned to a client.

definitions.definition: An employee who performs only companion or sitter tasks for clients under the client's service plan and who is not also qualified and assigned as a nurse or PCA.
The non-personal-care tasks defined in Rule 111-8-65-.03(c) and listed in policy SVC-03, performed according to the client's service plan.

Observed, documented performance of a skill or knowledge area to the satisfaction of the RN Supervisor or Supervisor, by demonstration or written/oral evaluation, in place of completed classroom training.
A companion or sitter who also meets the qualifications of a PCA (ADM-11) or a licensed nurse (ADM-10), with the qualification documented in the personnel file.

procedures: The Administrator maintains a written job description for companions and sitters. It limits the position to companion or sitter tasks and requires the ability to read, write, follow instructions and complete reports.

At application, the Administrator or designee confirms literacy. The applicant reads a written client instruction aloud or explains it, and writes a short sample visit note. The result is recorded on the hiring checklist.
The agency completes the background check, registry and health screening steps required by PER-01 and ADM-07 before the applicant has client contact.

Before any client assignment, the Supervisor determines for each of the seven required areas whether the employee has completed training or must demonstrate competency. The areas are the needs of elderly, handicapped or convalescing persons; meal preparation and serving; transport and escort; housekeeping and sanitation; home safety; medical emergencies; and infection control.

Where the employee presents prior training, the Supervisor reviews proof such as a certificate, transcript or course outline. The Supervisor accepts it only if it covers the subject, and copies it to the personnel file.

Where the employee has no proof of training, the RN Supervisor or Supervisor conducts a competency demonstration using the agency's Companion/Sitter Competency Checklist. This includes observed meal preparation and serving, hand hygiene and sanitation steps, a home-safety walk-through, a transport/escort scenario, and a medical-emergency response scenario.
The Supervisor signs and dates the checklist. Any area not passed is retrained and re-demonstrated before the employee is assigned.
The Administrator files the training certificates and signed competency checklist in the personnel file and records the completion date for each of the seven areas on the personnel training log.
The employee completes agency orientation under ADM-13 and the written competency evaluation under ADM-09 before client contact.
The scheduler assigns the employee only to clients whose service plan calls for companion or sitter tasks (SVC-03). The service plan assignment sheet states the tasks the employee may perform.

If a client or family member asks a companion or sitter to perform a personal care or nursing task, the employee declines politely, does not perform the task, and calls the Supervisor the same day. The Supervisor decides whether the service plan needs review under PLN-01 or whether a qualified PCA or nurse must be assigned.

If the agency wants to use an employee for both companion and personal care work, the Administrator first verifies and documents that the employee meets the PCA requirements in ADM-11 (or the nurse requirements in ADM-10) before any personal care assignment.
The companion or sitter reports client needs, changes in condition and observed problems to the Supervisor, and completes the daily documentation required by SVC-09 for every visit.
The Supervisor supervises companion and sitter services under SVC-07, including the required home visits and an annual written evaluation by direct observation.
The Administrator provides at least 8 clock hours of in-service training each year after the first year of employment under ADM-14, including refreshers on the required areas.

The Administrator addresses any companion or sitter performing tasks outside the service plan or beyond their qualifications through documented corrective action, up to removal from client assignments, and reports as required by LIC-06 and SAF-02.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures no companion or sitter works with clients until all requirements are verified and documented; maintains job descriptions and personnel files.
Verifies prior training, conducts and signs competency demonstrations, assigns tasks per the service plan, and supervises services.
Assigns companions and sitters only to clients whose service plans call for companion or sitter tasks.
Performs only assigned companion or sitter tasks, declines other tasks, completes reports and visit documentation, and reports client needs and changes to the Supervisor.

documentation: Hiring checklist showing the literacy check (read, write, follow instructions, complete reports)
Training certificates or signed Companion/Sitter Competency Checklist covering all seven required areas
Personnel training log with completion dates
Dual-qualification documentation (PCA or nurse), if applicable
Corrective action records for out-of-scope tasks

policies.title: Orientation Before Working With Clients
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor/Supervisors, and all employees and contracted individuals who provide services to clients of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every person who provides services to clients is oriented to the agency's policies, client rights, assigned duties, reporting and emergency procedures, and exposure-reporting obligations before any client contact.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.09(6) (Staff Training) and Rule 111-8-65-.09(6)(a)1-4 (Orientation). Before working with clients, every employee hired or used who provides services to clients is oriented under this policy. Further training follows under ADM-14. Orientation includes instruction in: (1) Rule .09(6)(a)1: the agency's written policies and procedures on its scope of services and the types of clients it serves (Rule .09(1), policy ADM-01), client rights and responsibilities and complaints (Rule .12, policies CR-01 and CR-02), and other policies relevant to the employee's range of duties; (2) Rule .09(6)(a)2: the employee's assigned duties and responsibilities; (3) Rule .09(6)(a)3: reporting client progress and problems to supervisory personnel, and procedures for handling medical emergencies or other incidents that affect delivery of services under the client's service plan; and (4) Rule .09(6)(a)4: the employee's obligation to report known exposure to tuberculosis and hepatitis to the employer. Employees with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials also receive the bloodborne pathogens training required by OSHA, 29 CFR 1910.1030, as part of orientation and infection control training (SAF-03). No employee is scheduled for or placed with a client until orientation is complete and the signed checklist is in the personnel file.

definitions.definition: The initial instruction, completed before any client contact, covering the four content areas required by Rule 111-8-65-.09(6)(a).
Any in-person, telephone or virtual interaction with a client for the purpose of delivering or shadowing services, other than the pre-service shadowing described in this policy.
Known exposure to, or diagnosis of, tuberculosis or hepatitis that the employee must report to the employer.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a written Orientation Program and checklist covering all four required content areas. The Administrator reviews and updates them at the annual policy review (GB-01).
When an offer is accepted, the Administrator or designee schedules orientation before the employee's first client assignment and records the date on the hire checklist.
The trainer reviews with the employee the agency's written policies on scope of services and types of clients served (ADM-01) and gives the employee access to the full Policy and Procedure Manual.
The trainer reviews client rights and responsibilities and the complaint process (CR-01, CR-02), including how an employee should respond when a client or family member voices a complaint.

The trainer reviews the employee's assigned duties, using the job description, the tasks the employee is qualified to perform (SVC-01, SVC-02 or SVC-03) and the limits of the employee's role. The employee receives a copy of the job description.

The trainer reviews how to report client progress, needs, changes in condition and observed problems to the Supervisor, including the on-call process (SVC-08), and how to use the daily documentation forms (SVC-09).
The trainer reviews procedures for medical emergencies and other incidents in the home (SAF-07, SAF-02), including when to call 911, whom to notify next, and what to document.

The trainer explains the employee's obligation to report known exposure to tuberculosis or hepatitis to the employer immediately, and to whom to report. The employee learns that the agency will not permit an exposed or diagnosed employee to serve clients until determined not to be contagious (SVC-04).
Employees with occupational exposure complete bloodborne pathogens training consistent with 29 CFR 1910.1030 as part of infection control instruction (SAF-03), before client contact.
The trainer also covers abuse, neglect and exploitation reporting (SAF-01), confidentiality (CR-03), and professional boundaries (PER-03), because these are relevant to every employee's duties.
The trainer verifies understanding through questions or a short written or verbal check, and re-teaches any topic the employee does not understand.
The employee and trainer sign and date the Orientation Checklist, listing each topic and the date completed.

The Administrator verifies the checklist is complete and filed in the personnel file before releasing the employee to the scheduler for any client assignment. The scheduler does not assign anyone whose orientation is not marked complete.
Contracted individuals providing services on the agency's behalf complete the same orientation before their first client contact (ADM-15).

The Administrator audits personnel files at least annually, and when a new employee is hired, to confirm every employee has a completed orientation checklist dated before the first client contact. Gaps are corrected immediately and the employee is removed from client assignment until corrected.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the orientation program and checklist, verifies completion before first client assignment, and audits files.
Delivers or oversees orientation content on duties, reporting and emergencies; confirms employee understanding.
Does not schedule any employee for client contact until the Administrator confirms orientation is complete.
Attends orientation, asks questions, signs the checklist, and reports known TB or hepatitis exposure to the employer.

documentation: Signed and dated Orientation Checklist listing all four required content areas and the OSHA bloodborne pathogens training, kept in the personnel file
Written Orientation Program and training materials
Job description acknowledged by the employee
Employee acknowledgment of receipt of the Policy and Procedure Manual
Annual personnel file audit record

policies.title: Annual In-Service Training (8 Clock Hours)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor/Supervisors, and all employees of [AGENCY NAME] who have completed their first year of employment
policies.purpose: To make sure each employee receives at least eight clock hours of job-related training every year after the first year of employment, and that the hours are tracked and documented.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.09(6)(b) (Annual Additional Training). [AGENCY NAME] provides a minimum of eight (8) clock hours of training or instruction annually to each employee after the first year of employment. Employees who were hired before the effective date of the rules are also required to receive eight clock hours annually beginning with that effective date. The training must be in subjects that relate to the employee's assigned duties and responsibilities. The Administrator tracks hours and topics by employee, and an employee who has not completed the required hours is not considered to be in compliance until the shortfall is made up and documented.

definitions.definition: Sixty minutes of actual instruction or training, excluding meals, breaks and travel.
The 12-month period beginning on the employee's first anniversary of hire, and each anniversary after that. Each period requires at least 8 clock hours.
Instruction related to the employee's assigned duties, delivered by the agency or an outside provider, in person, live online or by self-study with a documented check of understanding.

procedures: In January of each year, the Administrator and RN Supervisor prepare an annual in-service training plan, based on the services the agency offers, the results of supervisory evaluations (SVC-04), incident trends (SAF-02) and quality improvement findings (SVC-10).

The plan includes topics tied to employees' duties. Examples are infection control, client rights, abuse/neglect/exploitation reporting, emergency response, safe body mechanics and transfers, care for clients with dementia, documentation, boundaries and service plan tasks.
The Administrator sets up a Training Tracker for each employee that lists hire date, first anniversary date, each training year, hours completed, topics, date, trainer and proof of attendance.
The Administrator reviews the tracker monthly and identifies employees whose first anniversary is coming up or who have not completed 8 hours with 90 days left in the training year.
At least 60 days before the end of an employee's training year, the Administrator notifies any employee with fewer than 8 hours and schedules the remaining training.
Each session is led by a qualified trainer. The RN Supervisor reviews clinical content. For outside courses, the Administrator checks that the content relates to the employee's duties.
The agency counts only actual instructional time toward the 8 clock hours. Orientation (ADM-13) and the 40-hour PCA program (ADM-11) are not counted toward the annual 8 hours.

Employees sign an attendance sheet or submit a certificate that states the topic, date, length in clock hours and trainer or provider. Self-study counts only when a short test or written summary is completed and kept.
Training is conducted on paid time under PER-02. The Administrator treats training hours as hours worked for wage and overtime purposes.
The Administrator files all attendance records and certificates in the personnel file within 7 days of the training and updates the tracker.

If an employee has not completed 8 hours by the end of the training year, the Administrator documents the reason, schedules makeup training within 30 days, and may restrict the employee from new assignments until training is made up.
Employees hired before the effective date of the rule, if any, follow the same 8-hour annual requirement.
The Administrator reports annual completion rates to the governing body at the annual review (GB-01), and the quality improvement program (SVC-10) uses training gaps to set the next year's topics.
Training records are kept for the length of employment and for at least the period required by ADM-07, so that they are available to DCH surveyors during inspections (LIC-03).

responsibilities.duty: Develops the annual plan, maintains the tracker, schedules makeup training and verifies completion for every employee.
Reviews and delivers clinical in-service content and recommends topics based on supervisory evaluations.
Attends scheduled training, turns in certificates and signs attendance sheets, and completes at least 8 clock hours each training year.
Reviews annual in-service completion at the annual policy review.

documentation: Annual in-service training plan
Per-employee Training Tracker with training year, hours, topics, dates and trainers
Attendance sheets and certificates
Test or written summary for self-study courses
Makeup training records and corrective notes
Annual completion report to the governing body

policies.title: Contracted Services and Independent Contractors
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor/Supervisors, and any independent contractor, individual or agent who provides services on behalf of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure that any service arranged through an independent contractor, individual or agent is set out in writing, meets the rules, is provided by qualified persons, and is supervised by the agency's own supervisor.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.09(7) (Contracted Services). If [AGENCY NAME] arranges with independent contractors, individuals or agents to provide any authorized private home care services on its behalf in any way, the arrangement is set out in writing and details the services to be provided. The agency assures that each contractor, individual or agent follows the provisions of the Georgia private home care rules and is qualified to provide the services. Contracted services are supervised under Rule .10(2) (Supervision of Services) by a supervisor of the licensed agency, and the agency remains responsible for the services delivered. It is the agency's policy to employ its personal care assistants, companions and sitters as W-2 employees. Contracts are limited to licensed professionals, such as a nurse, where the agency has a documented need. The Administrator monitors the status of the proposed HB 183 revision, which would limit contractors to professionals licensed under Title 43. Its adoption status has not been verified, and the agency will adjust this policy if it is adopted.

definitions.definition: Any private home care service delivered to a client on the agency's behalf by an independent contractor, individual or agent rather than an agency employee.
A person or entity who is engaged by written agreement to provide services and who is not an employee of the agency.
A qualified supervisor employed by [AGENCY NAME] who supervises contracted services in the same manner as employee services under Rule .10(2).

procedures: Before engaging any contractor, the Administrator documents the reason, the services needed, and why the service cannot be delivered by an agency employee.

The Administrator confirms that the contractor holds the license or qualification that the service requires. For nursing, the Administrator verifies an active Georgia RN or LPN license against the state licensing board record and keeps a dated copy of the verification.

The Administrator obtains a written agreement signed by both parties before any client contact. It names the services to be provided, the clients or client types, the rates, the term and the termination process.
The agreement requires the contractor to follow all provisions of Georgia Rule 111-8-65 and the agency's policies, including client rights, confidentiality, abuse/neglect reporting and documentation.

The agreement requires the contractor to be supervised by [AGENCY NAME]'s RN Supervisor or Supervisor, including participation in supervisory home visits and written evaluations as required by SVC-04 through SVC-07.

The agreement requires the contractor to complete agency orientation (ADM-13), background check and registry screening (PER-01), health screening (ADM-07) and proof of TB or hepatitis exposure reporting before the first client visit.

The agreement requires the contractor to complete the same daily service documentation as employees (SVC-09) and to report client needs, changes in condition, incidents and emergencies to the Supervisor immediately (SAF-02, SAF-07).
The agreement requires the contractor to maintain professional liability insurance, where applicable, and the Administrator keeps a certificate on file.

The Administrator keeps a contractor file with the signed agreement, license verification, orientation checklist, background check result, health screening documents, insurance certificate and annual evaluation.
The Supervisor assigns contracted services in the service plan (PLN-01), schedules supervisory visits and observes the contractor's work at least annually.
The Supervisor documents any concern, such as a missed visit, quality problem or complaint, and tells the Administrator within one business day.
The Administrator takes corrective action, including termination of the agreement, if the contractor does not follow the rules or the agreement, and reports as required by LIC-06 and SAF-01.
The Administrator reviews each contractor agreement at least annually, and presents the list of active contractors and services at the governing body's annual review (GB-01).

The Administrator monitors DCH notices and rule changes, including HB 183, for effects on contracting. Aides, companions and sitters continue to be hired as W-2 employees, and the Administrator reports any change in this policy to the governing body.

responsibilities.duty: Approves contractors, executes written agreements, verifies qualifications, maintains contractor files and monitors rule changes.
Supervises contracted services under Rule .10(2), observes and evaluates the contractor, and reports concerns.
Follows the rules and agency policies, maintains required licensure and documentation, and reports client changes and incidents promptly.
Reviews contracted services annually.

documentation: Signed written contractor agreement detailing the services
License or qualification verification with date
Contractor orientation, background check and health screening records
Insurance certificate, if applicable
Supervisory visit notes and annual written evaluation
Annual contractor review for the governing body

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Nursing Services and RN Supervisor
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor [RN SUPERVISOR NAME], registered nurses and licensed practical nurses of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define how [AGENCY NAME] delivers nursing services, if offered, by licensed nurses under the supervision of a fully licensed Georgia registered nurse and according to each client's service plan.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.10(1)(a)1(i)-(iv) (Nursing Services) and Rule 111-8-65-.10(2)(a) (Supervision of Nursing Services). [AGENCY NAME] offers nursing services only while it employs a fully licensed Georgia registered professional nurse (RN) to supervise those services and the employees who provide them. Nursing services are provided only by a licensed RN or a licensed practical nurse (LPN), under the direction of the RN Supervisor, in accordance with the scope of nursing practice laws and rules and the client's service plan. Nursing services include: (i) regularly assessing the nursing needs of the client; (ii) participating in establishing and implementing the client's service plan; (iii) providing nursing services as needed and in accordance with the service plan; and (iv) reporting problems and progress of the client to the supervisor or the client's personal physician. The RN Supervisor may perform other duties as long as he or she can fulfill the supervisory responsibilities in the rules. The RN Supervisor completes the client's service plan under Rule .11 and policy PLN-01, in coordination with the staff who will provide the client's services. If the agency has no fully licensed Georgia RN supervisor, it does not accept clients who need nursing services and does not provide them.

definitions.definition: Services provided by a licensed RN or LPN within the scope of nursing practice laws and the client's service plan, including assessment, participation in the service plan, nursing care as planned, and reporting of problems and progress.
A fully licensed Georgia registered professional nurse employed by [AGENCY NAME] to supervise nursing services and the employees who provide them.
The written plan completed by the supervisor for each client under Rule .11 (PLN-01) that identifies the services to be provided.

procedures: Before offering nursing services, the Administrator verifies that [RN SUPERVISOR NAME] holds a current, fully licensed Georgia RN license, and keeps a dated primary-source verification in the personnel file (ADM-10).

The Administrator re-verifies the RN Supervisor's license at each renewal period and at least annually, and keeps the record. If the license lapses or is restricted, the Administrator immediately suspends acceptance of nursing clients, arranges an interim qualified RN supervisor, and notifies the governing body.
The Administrator verifies the licenses of all RNs and LPNs before hire or assignment (ADM-10) and keeps verification at each renewal.

At intake (OPS-01), the RN Supervisor or designated RN determines whether a prospective client needs nursing services and whether the agency can meet those needs with its current nursing staff (ADM-01).

The RN Supervisor completes the client's service plan under PLN-01 in coordination with the nurses and other staff who will provide care, and the plan lists the specific nursing services to be provided and their frequency.
Each assigned nurse regularly assesses the nursing needs of the client at the frequency the service plan states, and documents each assessment in the client record.

The nurse takes part in establishing the service plan, provides the nursing services that are needed and listed in the plan, and works within the scope of practice for the nurse's license. The nurse does not perform any act outside that scope or outside the service plan.
An LPN works under the direction of the RN Supervisor, who reviews the LPN's assessments and documentation, and provides direction by phone or in person as needed.

The nurse reports problems and progress of the client to the RN Supervisor or the client's personal physician. A significant change in condition or an emergency is reported immediately under SAF-07, and the nurse follows the physician's instructions where a physician is contacted.
The nurse completes daily documentation of services at each visit (SVC-09) and gives it to the RN Supervisor within the time set by policy.
The RN Supervisor supervises nursing staff and conducts supervisory visits and an annual written evaluation by direct observation of each nurse, as required by SVC-04.
The RN Supervisor reviews the service plan whenever the client's condition changes and at the intervals in PLN-01, and revises the plan in coordination with the client and the nursing staff.

The RN Supervisor may perform other duties, such as scheduling or administration, only if these do not prevent timely supervision of all nursing clients. The Administrator monitors the supervisor's workload and assigns additional supervisory support when needed.
Nurses may also perform personal care tasks within the service plan (SVC-02).
The Administrator includes nursing service delivery in the quality improvement program (SVC-10) and reports findings to the governing body.

responsibilities.duty: Employs a fully licensed Georgia RN supervisor before offering nursing services, verifies all nurse licenses, and suspends nursing acceptance if no qualified RN supervisor is available.
Supervises nursing services and staff, completes service plans with the staff who will deliver care, reviews assessments and documentation, and evaluates nurses annually.
Assesses client nursing needs, takes part in the service plan, provides nursing within the scope of practice and the plan, and reports problems and progress to the supervisor or physician.
Ensures the agency does not offer nursing services without a qualified RN supervisor.

documentation: Dated license verifications for the RN Supervisor, RNs and LPNs
Service plans listing nursing services, completed by the RN Supervisor
Nursing assessments and visit documentation in the client record
Records of reports to the supervisor or physician
Supervisory visit notes and annual written evaluations of nursing staff

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Personal Care Tasks
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor/Supervisors, Personal Care Assistants (PCAs) and licensed nurses of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure personal care tasks are performed only by qualified PCAs or licensed nurses, under supervision and according to the client's service plan, and that changes in a client's condition and observed problems are reported.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.10(1)(b) (Personal Care Tasks). Personal care tasks, as defined in Rule .03(n), such as bathing, toileting, grooming, shaving, dental care, dressing and eating assistance, are performed, at a minimum, by a qualified PCA under the direction of a supervisor and in accordance with the client's service plan. Licensed nurses are also authorized to perform personal care tasks. In addition to following the service plan, a PCA must report on the personal care needs of the client, on changes in the client's condition, and on any observed problems that affect the client. No employee performs a task that is not in the client's service plan or that is beyond the employee's training and qualifications. Companions and sitters do not perform personal care tasks (ADM-12).

definitions.definition: The hands-on tasks defined in Rule 111-8-65-.03(n), including bathing, toileting, grooming, shaving, dental care, dressing and assistance with eating.
An employee who meets the PCA qualifications and training requirements in policy ADM-11, including the 40-hour training program or an equivalent credential.
The written plan that lists each client's services, completed by the supervisor under PLN-01.

procedures: The Administrator confirms that each PCA meets the qualifications in ADM-11 and has completed orientation (ADM-13) before the PCA is assigned to any client. The Administrator keeps proof in the personnel file.
At intake and assessment (OPS-01), the Supervisor identifies which personal care tasks the client needs and how often, and whether the client is medically frail or compromised (SVC-05).
The Supervisor writes the service plan under PLN-01 listing each personal care task, frequency, special instructions, client preferences and safety precautions.
The Supervisor gives the assigned PCA a copy of the service plan or task sheet, and reviews it with the PCA before the first visit. The PCA's access to the plan is available at each visit.
The scheduler assigns only qualified PCAs or licensed nurses to clients with personal care tasks in the service plan (OPS-02).
At each visit, the PCA performs only the personal care tasks listed in the service plan and within his or her training, following client preferences, dignity and privacy (CR-01).

If a client asks for a task that is not in the service plan or that the PCA has not been trained to do, the PCA politely declines, explains that the Supervisor will review the request, and calls the Supervisor the same day. The Supervisor decides whether to amend the service plan under PLN-01.
If a task cannot be done safely, for example because equipment is missing or the client's condition has changed, the PCA stops, keeps the client safe and calls the Supervisor right away.

The PCA reports to the Supervisor the client's personal care needs, any change in the client's condition and any problem observed, such as skin changes, falls, confusion, refusal of care, pain, poor intake or unsafe conditions. Routine reports are made by the end of the visit or shift, and urgent matters are reported immediately (SAF-07).
In an emergency, the PCA calls 911 first and then notifies the Supervisor or on-call representative (SVC-08, SAF-07).
The PCA uses standard precautions and hand hygiene during personal care (SAF-03).
The PCA documents the tasks performed at every visit on the daily record (SVC-09), including any task not completed and the reason, and any reports made to the Supervisor.

The Supervisor reviews the PCA's documentation, follows up on every reported change or problem within one business day (sooner for urgent matters), and records the follow-up in the client record. The follow-up may be a service plan review, a call to the client's physician or family, or a request for further evaluation.
The Supervisor supervises personal care services under SVC-05 and SVC-06, including home visits every 92 days, and evaluates each PCA in writing at least annually by direct observation (SVC-04).
The Administrator reviews documented out-of-scope task performance, and takes corrective action up to removal from assignments, with retraining before reassignment.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures only qualified PCAs and nurses are assigned to personal care and that corrective action is taken for out-of-scope tasks.
Writes the service plan, reviews it with the PCA, follows up on reports of changes or problems, and supervises and evaluates PCAs.
Performs only assigned personal care tasks within training, reports needs, changes in condition and observed problems, and documents each visit.
Assigns qualified personnel only to clients needing personal care tasks.

documentation: Service plan listing personal care tasks and frequency
PCA qualification and training records (ADM-11) in the personnel file
Daily documentation of tasks performed and tasks not completed
Records of PCA reports of needs, changes in condition and problems, and Supervisor follow-up
Supervisory visit notes and annual written evaluations
Corrective action records for out-of-scope tasks

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Companion or Sitter Tasks
policies.applies_to: Companions, sitters, PCAs and nurses who perform companion or sitter tasks; supervisors; the Administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure companion or sitter tasks are performed only by qualified staff, under a qualified supervisor, according to the client's service plan, and that staff report client needs, changes in condition and observed problems.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides companion or sitter tasks as a category of private home care services. This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.10(1)(c) — Companion or Sitter Tasks. Companion or sitter tasks are performed at a minimum by a qualified companion or sitter, working under the direction of a qualified supervisor as required by Georgia rules and in accordance with the client's written service plan. A qualified PCA or a licensed nurse may also perform these tasks. Companion or sitter tasks include transport and escort, meal preparation and serving, and household tasks essential to the client's cleanliness and safety, as defined in the state's definitions of companion or sitter tasks and related terms. A companion or sitter must follow the service plan and must also report on the needs of the client, changes in the client's condition, and any observed problems that affect the client. A staff member working only as a companion or sitter may not perform personal care tasks or nursing services. Personal care for a client is assigned only to a qualified PCA or nurse under SVC-02, and nursing only to a licensed nurse under SVC-01.

definitions.definition: Non-personal-care, non-nursing tasks defined in the state rule definitions, including transport and escort, meal preparation and serving, and household tasks essential to the client's cleanliness and safety.
An employee who has met the hiring, competency, orientation and background check requirements in ADM-09, ADM-12, ADM-13 and PER-01 before working alone with a client.
An RN, LPN, the Administrator, or another staff member assigned responsibility for supervising the delivery of companion or sitter care (see SVC-07).
The written plan developed and reviewed under PLN-01 that lists the tasks, schedule and goals for each client.

Accompanying or driving a client to appointments or errands. When the employee drives a vehicle not owned by the client, the agency obtains a client waiver of claims or makes reasonable efforts to confirm motor vehicle insurance.

procedures: At intake, the supervisor determines from the assessment (OPS-01) whether the client needs companion or sitter tasks only, or also needs personal care or nursing. The supervisor records the finding in the client record.
The supervisor lists each companion or sitter task the client is to receive on the service plan (PLN-01). Only tasks listed on the plan may be performed.

The scheduler assigns only staff whose personnel file shows they are qualified: a companion or sitter, or a PCA or nurse. The file must show completed background check, competency evaluation, orientation and required training (ADM-09, ADM-11, ADM-12, ADM-13, PER-01).

Before the first visit, the supervisor reviews the service plan with the assigned companion or sitter. The review covers the tasks, the schedule, client preferences, safety concerns and who to call. The employee signs a copy of the plan acknowledgement.
The companion or sitter performs only the tasks on the service plan. Tasks outside the plan are done only after the supervisor approves a plan revision (ADM-03, PLN-01).

If a client asks a companion or sitter for bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring, feeding assistance, hands-on grooming, medication handling beyond what the plan allows, or any nursing task, the employee politely declines. The employee notifies the supervisor the same day. The supervisor then reassesses the client and, if needed, assigns a qualified PCA or nurse and revises the plan.

Before the agency provides transport or escort in a vehicle the client does not own, the supervisor confirms that the employee has a valid driver's license. The supervisor also confirms that either a signed client waiver of claims is on file or reasonable efforts to verify the employee's motor vehicle insurance are documented. SAF-06 applies.

For meal preparation and serving, the employee follows any diet instructions on the service plan, uses safe food handling under SAF-03, and reports to the supervisor any eating or swallowing problem, or any refusal to eat, that the client has not shown before.

For household tasks, the employee performs only those essential to the client's cleanliness and safety, such as dishes, laundry, trash and light cleaning of areas used by the client. The employee follows SAF-05 for chemicals and equipment.
Companions and sitters do not handle client money, cards or checks except as permitted by CR-04, which includes any bonding requirement for unlimited access to funds.

The companion or sitter reports to the supervisor by phone on the same day any change in the client's condition (for example, new confusion, a fall, refusal of food or fluids, new injury or illness) or any observed problem (for example, unsafe conditions in the home, signs of abuse, neglect or exploitation, or missing supplies). In an emergency, the employee calls 911 first and then the supervisor (SAF-07). Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported under SAF-01.
The employee records each visit's tasks and observations in the daily service record (SVC-09). The record includes any change in condition or problem reported and the name of the supervisor notified.

The supervisor reviews each report on the day received, decides on follow-up, which may include a nurse consultation, an earlier supervisory visit, a service plan revision or a referral. The supervisor documents the follow-up in the client record.
The supervisor supervises companion or sitter services under SVC-07, including home visits at least every 122 days, and evaluates each employee in writing at least annually under SVC-04.
The Administrator reviews the companion and sitter task list, and any task requests that had to be declined, at least annually as part of the quality improvement program (SVC-10).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures only qualified staff are assigned companion or sitter tasks, that a qualified supervisor is designated, and that this policy is followed.

responsibilities.role: Supervisor (RN, LPN, Administrator or assigned staff)
responsibilities.duty: Assesses need, writes the service plan, briefs staff, receives reports of changes and problems, and documents follow-up.
Assigns only qualified staff and does not schedule companions or sitters for personal care or nursing visits.
Performs only the tasks on the service plan, declines tasks outside the plan, and reports client needs, changes in condition and observed problems the same day.

documentation: Client assessment and service plan listing companion or sitter tasks
Employee acknowledgement of the service plan
Daily service records, including observations and reports (SVC-09)
Supervisor follow-up notes in the client record
Client waiver of claims or documentation of insurance verification for transport
Personnel file showing qualifications of the assigned employee

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Supervision of Services, Annual Written Evaluation and Exposure Exclusion
policies.applies_to: All employees and contractors who provide services to clients; all supervisors; the Administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure all services are supervised by qualified staff, every service staff member is evaluated in writing at least once a year by direct observation or demonstration, and no employee who may be contagious with tuberculosis or hepatitis serves clients.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.10(2) — Supervision of Services. [AGENCY NAME] supervises all services through qualified agency staff. Each staff member who provides services to a client is evaluated in writing by his or her supervisor at least annually, either through direct observation or demonstration, on the job tasks the staff member is required to perform. No supervisor will knowingly permit an employee who has been exposed to tuberculosis or hepatitis, or who has been diagnosed with either, to provide services to clients until it is determined that the employee is not contagious. Where the agency offers nursing, it employs a fully licensed Georgia RN as supervisor (SVC-01). Supervisors may perform other duties as long as they can fulfill their supervisory duties.

definitions.definition: A staff member the agency has determined to be qualified by education, training and experience to supervise the services assigned to them, as described in SVC-05 and SVC-07.
The supervisor watches the employee perform the job tasks, either with a client in the home or as a return demonstration, and rates the performance.
A written evaluation completed at least once in every 12-month period.
Known contact with a person with active tuberculosis or infectious hepatitis in a way that creates a risk of transmission, or a diagnosis of either disease.

procedures: The Administrator designates in writing a qualified supervisor for each service type: nursing, personal care, and companion or sitter. Each supervisor's qualifications are filed under ADM-04 and ADM-09 and noted in a supervisor roster.
The roster assigns each employee and contractor who serves clients to a named supervisor. The Administrator updates the roster whenever staff or assignments change.
Supervisors review service plans with assigned staff at the start of service, are available by phone during service hours, and respond to staff reports of problems the same day.
Supervisors conduct home visits and other supervisory activities required by SVC-05, SVC-06, SVC-07 and SVC-08.

Within the first 30 days after an employee begins working independently with clients, the supervisor does a first observation of the employee performing the job tasks and documents it. This agency practice helps correct problems early.

At least once every 12 months, the supervisor evaluates each staff member in writing by direct observation or demonstration of the job tasks the person is required to perform. The Administrator tracks due dates on the evaluation tracking log and sends reminders 30 days in advance.

The evaluation form lists the specific tasks from the employee's job description and service plans (for example, safe transfers, infection control, meal preparation, documentation, reporting changes in condition). The supervisor marks each task as satisfactory or needs improvement, notes the method (observation or demonstration), and dates and signs the form. The employee also signs.

When a task is rated needs improvement, the supervisor documents coaching or retraining, sets a re-check date within 30 days, and documents the re-check. An employee who cannot perform a task safely is not assigned that task until the supervisor documents competence.
Evaluations are filed in the employee's personnel record (ADM-07). Evaluation results are also used in the quality improvement program (SVC-10).

Any employee who has been exposed to, or diagnosed with, tuberculosis or hepatitis must tell the Administrator before the next scheduled shift. This duty is explained at orientation (ADM-13) and in the employee handbook.

If a supervisor learns of an exposure or diagnosis from any source, the supervisor immediately notifies the Administrator and does not assign the employee to client care. The Administrator removes the employee from the client schedule and arranges coverage so clients are not left without service (OPS-02).

The Administrator requires the employee to obtain written clearance from a physician, nurse practitioner or the local public health department stating that the employee is not contagious. The employee returns to client care only after the written clearance is received, reviewed by the Administrator and filed in the confidential health section of the personnel record.

The Administrator treats employee medical information as confidential, keeps it separate from the general personnel file, and shares it only with those who need it to carry out this policy. The Administrator considers reasonable accommodations, such as non-client duties, under applicable employment laws.
If clients may have been exposed, the Administrator consults the local health department and follows its guidance. Notifications are made under SAF-03 and LIC-06 as applicable.
The Administrator reviews the evaluation tracking log monthly. An employee whose evaluation is overdue is not scheduled for new client assignments until the evaluation is completed.

responsibilities.duty: Designates supervisors, maintains the supervision roster and evaluation tracking log, and removes and returns employees under the exposure rule.
Supervises assigned staff, completes written annual evaluations by observation or demonstration, and documents coaching and re-checks.
Reports exposure to or diagnosis of tuberculosis or hepatitis immediately, participates in evaluations, and carries out corrective actions.

documentation: Supervisor roster and qualifications
Annual written evaluation forms signed by the supervisor and employee
Evaluation tracking log
Corrective action and re-check notes
Written clearance and exclusion/return dates (confidential health file)

policies.category: Rule .10 Private Home Care Provider Services
policies.title: Supervision of Personal Care Tasks and Medically Frail or Compromised Clients
policies.applies_to: Supervisors, RNs, LPNs, PCAs, the Administrator and the intake team
policies.purpose: To make sure personal care tasks are supervised by qualified supervisors, that medically frail or compromised clients are identified at intake, and that those clients are supervised by a licensed nurse with an RN-developed initial service plan.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 111-8-65-.10(2)(b) — Supervision of Personal Care Tasks, and Rule 111-8-65-.10(2)(b)1 — Service Plan Completion by the Appropriate Supervisor. [AGENCY NAME] employs supervisors who have been determined to be qualified by education, training and experience to supervise personal care tasks in accordance with accepted standards of care. A licensed RN or LPN supervises personal care tasks for every client determined to be medically frail or medically compromised. If an LPN provides that supervision, the LPN reports to a licensed RN who remains responsible for developing and managing the service plan. The appropriate supervisor completes each client's service plan in coordination with the staff who will provide the services. For medically frail or compromised clients, a licensed RN completes the initial service plan. An LPN supervising the client may make later revisions, and the RN reviews each revision in a timely manner, which the agency defines as within 7 calendar days. A supervisor may perform other duties if he or she can fulfill the supervisory duties in this policy.

definitions.definition: A client whose health condition, as defined in the state rule definitions and determined by the agency RN under this policy, makes the client more vulnerable to a serious change in health, so that personal care needs nursing-level oversight.

A person whose education, training and experience, documented in the personnel file, show competence to supervise personal care tasks. For medically frail or compromised clients the supervisor must be a licensed RN or LPN.
The first written service plan developed before or at the start of services under PLN-01.
Review and signature by the RN within 7 calendar days of an LPN's revision.

procedures: The Administrator names qualified personal care supervisors and keeps their credentials, resume, license (if a nurse), training and experience in the supervisor file. The Administrator documents why each person is considered qualified.

The Administrator ensures an RN is available to serve as the agency's RN supervisor for any client determined to be medically frail or compromised. If no RN is on staff, the agency does not accept such clients.

During the intake assessment (OPS-01), the intake coordinator completes the Medical Frailty Screening section of the assessment before accepting any client who needs personal care. The screen asks about: unstable or poorly controlled chronic conditions; a hospital or skilled nursing stay in the past 30 days; complex medication regimens or high-risk medications; need for vital sign monitoring; wounds or pressure injuries; catheters, ostomies, feeding tubes, oxygen or other devices; swallowing problems or aspiration risk; repeated falls; and cognitive impairment with medical risk.

The RN reviews every screen, with a client visit when needed, and decides whether the client is medically frail or compromised under the state definition. When there is doubt, the client is treated as medically frail or compromised.

The RN records the determination, the reasons and the date in the client record at intake, and signs it. The determination is also marked on the client face sheet and the schedule so all staff and the on-call representative can see it (SVC-08).

For a client determined to be medically frail or compromised, the RN completes the initial service plan in coordination with the PCAs who will provide the services. The plan includes the personal care tasks, special instructions, signs and symptoms to report, and who to call.
For all other personal care clients, the appropriate qualified supervisor completes the service plan in coordination with the PCAs who will provide services, following PLN-01.

A licensed RN or LPN supervises personal care tasks for every medically frail or compromised client. If an LPN is assigned, the LPN's file shows the RN to whom the LPN reports. The RN remains responsible for developing and managing the service plan.

An LPN supervising a medically frail or compromised client may make later revisions to the service plan. The LPN documents each revision, with the date, reason and change, and sends it to the RN. The RN reviews and signs each revision within 7 calendar days and notes any changes ordered.

The supervisor reviews the service plan with each PCA before the first visit. The PCA signs the plan acknowledgement. The supervisor trains the PCA on any client-specific task before the PCA performs it alone.
The supervisor performs home visits under SVC-06 and consults with the PCA after any report of a change in condition (SAF-07).

The RN reassesses whether the client is medically frail or compromised at every supervisory home visit and whenever there is a hospitalization, a significant change in condition or a change in service level. If status changes, the RN updates the determination and service plan the same day, and the supervision level changes immediately.
The supervisor reports to the Administrator any client who may need services the agency cannot safely provide. The Administrator then follows OPS-03 on discharge and transfer.

The Administrator audits a sample of medically frail or compromised client records quarterly to confirm there is an RN-signed initial service plan, LPN revisions reviewed by the RN within 7 days, and RN or LPN supervision documented. Results go to the quality improvement program (SVC-10).

responsibilities.duty: Names qualified supervisors, ensures RN availability, and audits records for compliance.
Determines medical frailty, completes the initial service plan for medically frail or compromised clients, reviews LPN revisions within 7 days, and remains responsible for managing the plan.
